subject: Request: Switchover latency threshold / RTO variance for Crestline deployment

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Switchover latency threshold / RTO variance for Crestline deployment

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the demo was helpful. As we map Redwood into our business continuity plan there’s one item Compliance flagged that I wanted to raise formally: Crestline needs a documented commitment for cross-region switchover where the maximum allowable RTO is 15 minutes for the payment-router paths.

We understand Redwood’s standard warm-standby target is 30 minutes for the hosted tier; Crestline’s regulator will only accept 20 minutes or less unless there’s contractual mitigation. Our security and procurement teams asked whether Redwood can provide a temporary RTO variance and a technical fallback sequence that ensures no more than a 15 minute exposure for the payment path.

Attached: SLA-variance-form.pdf and an excerpt of our failover spec. Could you confirm the process, required approvals, and any additional cost or dedicated capacity expectations?

Best,
Mike Hsu
Director, Platform Ops
Crestline Bank
ops@crestlinebank.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Switchover latency threshold / RTO variance for Crestline deployment

Naomi / Dylan — quick technical readout below after an initial runbook review and perf sims.

Summary: For the payment-router routes only, achieving an operational RTO of <= 15 minutes is feasible but operationally constrained on Hosted unless we apply one or more of the following:

- Dedicated standby pool pinned to the customer (recommended): pre-warmed GPUs + pinned model variant and KV cache snapshot. Estimated incremental cost: two reserved inference nodes (A100-class equivalent) + storage for cache snapshots; ballpark $6k–9k/month depending on burst policy. Provisioning lead time: 3–5 business days for Dedicated capacity.
- Hybrid hosted with prioritized warm caches: we can reduce to ~18–20 minutes by increasing prefix cache retention and aggressive KV warm-up; still non-deterministic during region-wide outages with heavy global load.
- Architectural mitigation: route payment-router write traffic through a lightweight edge aggregator for very short-term buffering (adds a network hop but reduces critical state rebuild time). This requires small integration on their side (2–4 days).

Operational caveats: we need to document failback sequencing, automated health gates, and a canary window to avoid split-brain. Also recommend a 60–90 day probationary variance window with weekly readiness checks and a final decision point: either commit Dedicated capacity or fall back to the 30-minute baseline.

Draft variance language (high level):
"Redwood grants Crestline Bank a temporary RTO variance for payment-router traffic to a maximum recovery time of 15 minutes, subject to the implementation of a pinned dedicated standby pool or functionally equivalent mitigation as agreed in an attached runbook. This variance is effective for 60 days from execution and contingent upon weekly operational readiness reviews; failure to meet readiness gates will revert the effective RTO to Redwood's standard 30-minute switchover."

I’ve attached an updated failover diagram (failover-sequence-v2.png) and a sizing note (crestline-malp-specs.xlsx).

Happy to discuss; can be on a quick call if you want.

Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Thanks Naomi / Marcus — looping in a proposed next steps checklist for Procurement and CS to accept a 60-day variance: 

1) Execution: Procurement to sign the temporary variance addendum (we'll route via DocuSign). Draft addendum attached to the internal SharePoint link.
2) Provisioning: If Crestline chooses Dedicated, provision 2x nodes and validate cold-to-warm warm-up in staging (3 business days).
3) Runbook: Finalize automated failover runbook for payment-router traffic and publish to the Crestline DoD (read-only link).
4) Readiness checks: Weekly recovery drills during the variance window (logs and tracer snapshots to be uploaded to our shared S3).
5) Escalation: If a readiness check fails twice in a row, policy automatically reverts to 30-minute RTO until remediation.

Mike / Sarah — if Crestline agrees to the Dedicated option we can provide a formal cost/addendum and a target provisioning ETA. If they prefer to try hybrid hosted first we should document the non-deterministic risk and retain the right to revert.

Mike — would you be able to confirm procurement point-of-contact and whether Crestline has an internal change freeze window in July? That affects provisioning lead times.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
